_meta.source: Krumboltz, J. D. (2009), The Happenstance Learning Theory, Journal of Career Assessment 17(2)
_meta.notes: Planned happenstance holds that unplanned events shape careers more than plans do, and that certain dispositions decide whether a person can use an unplanned event. Here they are the currency of Journey mode: chance cards check dispositions, never grades. That substitution is the argument, made as a mechanic instead of a paragraph. These are surfaced when they are earned, not lectured up front.

dispositions.label: Curiosity
dispositions.body: Looking into things nobody set you. Asking in front of people.
dispositions.buildsWhen: you pick the option that teaches you something

dispositions.label: Persistence
dispositions.short: You stay with the hard thing.
dispositions.body: Not never struggling. What you do the week after it went badly.
dispositions.buildsWhen: you go back to something that went wrong

dispositions.label: Flexibility
dispositions.short: You change your mind on new facts.
dispositions.body: Adjusting the plan without treating it as a failure of the plan.
dispositions.buildsWhen: you drop a plan because you learned something

dispositions.label: Optimism
dispositions.body: Seeing a chance as possible rather than as something for other people.
dispositions.buildsWhen: you put yourself forward unsure of the outcome

dispositions.label: Risk taking
dispositions.body: Doing it before you feel ready, because the window is now.
dispositions.buildsWhen: you say yes to something uncomfortable

framing.headline: These are what move a life.
framing.body: Grades open particular doors at particular moments. Across forty years, what decides things is whether you noticed the chance.
